content:
I want a small app for keeping track of the books I'm reading.

When I open it I want to see what I'm currently reading and what I've finished. I want to add a book from a form, mark one as finished, and click through to a book to see its title, author and my notes. I'd like to be able to send someone a link to a single book.

Nothing fancy and no accounts. Skip the database, save the books to a JSON file so they're still there after a restart.

# My Books

A tiny reading tracker. No accounts, no database, no dependencies beyond Node.

```sh
npm start          # http://localhost:3000
npm test
```

Books are saved to `data/books.json` (created on first add). Set `BOOKS_FILE`
to store them somewhere else, and `PORT` to change the port.

## Pages

| Route                     | What it does                                         |
| ------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- |
| `GET /`                   | Currently reading, finished, and the add-a-book form |
| `POST /books`             | Add a book (title, author, optional notes)           |
| `GET /books/:id`          | One book — shareable link                            |
| `POST /books/:id/finish`  | Mark it finished                                     |
| `POST /books/:id/notes`   | Update its notes                                     |

content.text:
The app is built and working. Run it with `npm start` and open http://localhost:3000.

## What you get

- **Home page (`/`)** shows two lists, "Currently reading" and "Finished", with the add-a-book form (title, author, notes) underneath. Each title links to its own page.
- **Book page (`/books/<id>`)** shows the title, author, when it was added or finished, and your notes. There's a "Mark as finished" button (which disappears once finished), a small form to update the notes, and the full URL printed at the bottom so you can copy it and send it to someone. Anyone with the link can open it since there are no accounts.
- **Storage** is `data/books.json`, written atomically (temp file + rename) so a crash mid-save can't corrupt it. I verified end to end that adding two books, finishing one, killing the server and starting it again brings both back in the right lists. The `data/` folder is gitignored since it's your personal data; set `BOOKS_FILE` if you'd rather keep it elsewhere.

## Files

- `server.js` – the HTTP server and five routes (uses only Node built-ins, no Express)
- `lib/store.js` – reads/writes the JSON file; serializes writes so overlapping requests can't lose a book
- `lib/views.js` – the HTML templates, with everything escaped so a `<script>` in a title or note is displayed harmlessly
- `test/app.test.js` – 10 vitest tests covering persistence across a "restart", validation, finishing, notes, 404s, and concurrent adds; all passing via `npm test`
- `README.md` – the above in short form

One small thing I added beyond your list: the ability to edit notes from the book page, since notes on something you're mid-way through tend to grow. It's one textarea and one route; easy to remove if you'd rather not have it.

Nothing is committed yet; the changes are sitting in the working tree on `master` (`package-lock.json` was already there untracked before I started).
